messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 GPU memory pressure detected in us-west-2-pool-12. threshold=0.85, current=0.92. Auto-pager triggered. Job: runner/serve/kv-cache-sync

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: high-severity oncall page fired -> @alice-j (primary), @ben-s (secondary). Incident URL: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-4829

alice-j: ack'd. I'm looking. any customer impact reported?

ben-s: ack. will stand by to help with evictions/evacuations.

carla-eng: seeing a spike in kvcache evictions and cuda alloc failures in the logs: "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" across 3 nodes. Dump attached to incident.

alice-j: copying logs here: ```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] gpu0 cudaAlloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] kvcache: eviction triggered, freed=1.2GB
[2026-03-15T09:12:05Z] serve: request-id=abc123 latency=312ms
```

david-sre: rough cluster view: us-west-2-pool-12 utilization by instance: [0.92, 0.89, 0.95, 0.60, 0.88] — looks like two nodes above 0.9. Are these p3dn-type preemptible?

kevin-n: those are dedicated g5s (non-preemptible), but we ran a larger job yesterday for an eval that may have left warm KV state. Noted unusual long-running prefix caches.

alice-j: immediate mitigation plan: 1) drain traffic from the two highest-util nodes 2) trigger kv-cache sync/flush for largest tenants 3) spin up 2 new nodes behind pool autoscaler

ben-s: on it — starting drain command: `infractl node drain --pool us-west-2-pool-12 --nodes node-12-03,node-12-11`

ben-s: drain command issued. routing service reports routes draining. Expect reduced qps on those nodes in ~15s.

carla-eng: running a targeted kv-cache truncation for tenant=team-x per alice's plan: `kvctl flush --tenant team-x --max-bytes 1024M`

incident-bot: Auto-shedding policy executed: evicting 3 low-priority prefixes from KV cache on node-12-11. freed=3.1GB.

alice-j: good. spinning new nodes via autoscaler: requested 2 nodes. ETA ~90s.

david-sre: checking app-level errors: customers hitting 503s? Cloudfront logs show a brief spike of 502/503 errors for model-serving routes between 09:12:02 and 09:12:20 — estimate 120 requests failed. Tier: free-trial customers primarily.

kevin-n: confirming: fallback model variant was engaged for some requests (fallback to quantized-variant). That reduced some errors but increased token count and slightly higher mem.

alice-j: can we verify if our graceful degradation rules kicked in? console shows canary-fallback policy active for pool-12. Good.

ben-s: nodes drained and cordoned. Eviction pressure decreasing on node-12-11, node-12-03 still at 0.90.

pagerduty-bot: Update: PagerDuty incident PD-4829 escalated to oncall lead due to ongoing memory pressure after 10 minutes.

carla-eng: new nodes came up and joined pool at 09:13:45. kube events: `Added node node-12-22`, `Added node node-12-23`.

incident-bot: autoscaler: increased desired=12 -> 14 for us-west-2-pool-12.

alice-j: after new nodes attached, routing redistributed work. current pool utilization: [0.62, 0.57, 0.65, 0.59, 0.55, 0.60, 0.61, 0.58, 0.54, 0.63, 0.59, 0.60, 0.56, 0.57] — pressure normalized.

kevin-n: double-checking for memory leak: retention counts for kvcache prefixes show steady growth for tenant=team-x across the past 6 hours. Could be leaking pinned prefixes from recent evals.

alice-j: we should make this low-severity followup: 1) add TTL on pinned prefixes 2) audit eval job to ensure cleanup 3) add alert to track pinned-prefix growth rate.

ben-s: temporary mitigation: we've enabled auto-ttl=2h for new pinned prefixes in pool-12 config. Applied via `configctl set pool.us-west-2-pool-12.kv.pin_ttl=2h`

carla-eng: logs look stable now. no further cuda alloc failures since 09:14:10.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-4829 resolved by user alice-j. Resolution note: drained overloaded nodes, spun up extra capacity, applied kv-cache TTL, and mitigated customer impact.

alice-j: marking as resolved in PD. Postmortem owners: @carla-eng (root cause & remediation), @kevin-n (eval job audit), @david-sre (runbook updates).

david-sre: quick impact summary for postmortem: ~120 degraded requests, ~30 user-facing 5xx, affected primarily free-tier traffic during 09:12:02–09:13:00. No SLO breaches for premium customers.

carla-eng: saving diagnostic bundle to /var/run/incidents/PD-4829.tar.gz and uploading to incident tracker.

alice-j: followups added to backlog: - add kvcache pinned-prefix TTL by default - create alert for pinned-prefix growth > 1GB/hour - add a one-click drain + evacuate playbook for pool-level OOMs

ben-s: thumbs up. :thumbsup:

kevin-n: note for postmortem: consider limiting large eval jobs' warmup behavior on dedicated pools or set isolation flags.

incident-bot: Reminder: If you were paged and acknowledged this incident, please add a short oncall note with your name and action taken.

alice-j: oncall note: alice-j - drained nodes, coordinated kv flush, escalated to autoscaler, closed PD.
